headline: UK Inflation Rises to 3.5% Driven by Higher Motor Fuel Costs
summary: UK inflation increased to 3.5%, with higher motor fuel prices placing renewed pressure on household budgets and business operating costs.
why: Consumer price inflation measures changes in the cost of living and guides monetary policy decisions by the Bank of England regarding interest rates.

impacts.name: United Kingdom
impacts.why: Higher inflation erodes consumer purchasing power and increases pressure on the central bank to maintain restrictive interest rates.

why_moved: An unexpected tick-up in headline inflation to 3.5% raised concerns over persistent cost pressures facing UK consumers.
